steps.message:
Reconstruct the running machine as a NixOS 26.05 VM.

Start the reference with `/opt/runtime/reference start` and get a root shell
with `/opt/runtime/guest`. Ports: SSH 2222, HTTP 8080, HTTPS 8443. Its
configuration and behavior are the specification. Changes to it are disposable.

Graded: everything that affects how this machine is used by its tenants,
clients and operator. The goal is a drop-in replacement. Differences that come
only from the OS don't matter: kernel and version strings, package names, where system config files live, stock utilities nobody here is likely to need. Paths, names, identities, credentials, defaults and the commands people are likely to use for this machine's job do. No data migration: recreate what the server was
provisioned with (accounts, empty databases, seeded files), not data its users
added later.

Submit /app/submission/replica.nix, a plain NixOS module, plus local supporting
files. A minimal module is supplied. The harness imports it against the pinned
nixpkgs 26.05 at /opt/nixpkgs (revision in /opt/contract/flake.lock) with
Nix 2.35.4 on x86_64-linux and system.stateVersion = "26.05". No flake or lock
file is needed; use the normal pkgs/lib/config arguments. The build has no
network access.

The harness provides boot resources, port forwarding, root SSH and TLS: the server
certificate and key are installed at /etc/node/server.{crt,key}, and clients
trust /opt/contract/ca.crt.

Tools:
- `/opt/contract/check-replica [--syntax-only]` parses your Nix files and
  evaluates the full VM configuration without building or booting.
- `/opt/contract/build-replica` builds it. From a fresh writable directory, run
  /app/replica-vm/bin/run-*-vm. Candidate ports: SSH 3222, HTTP 9080,
  HTTPS 9443; `GUEST_SSH_PORT=3222 /opt/runtime/guest` opens its root shell.

The verifier boots a fresh disk from your submission, adds small programs and
data as the existing users, uses ordinary clients, and inspects effective
configuration. Passwords and fixture TLS keys on this lab machine are public.

Only /app/submission transfers to the verifier. Use real services. Do not copy
or embed the reference OS, fetch a remote answer, import paths outside your
submission and /opt/contract, or contact the reference at verification time.
I'll start by looking at the reference machine, the supplied minimal module, and the contract tools.

arguments.command: ls -la /app /app/submission /opt/contract /opt/runtime 2>&1; echo ---; cat /app/submission/replica.nix 2>/dev/null; echo ---; ls -la /app/replica-vm 2>&1 | head; echo ---; cat /opt/contract/flake.lock 2>/dev/null | head -50
arguments.description: Inspect app, contract, and runtime directories

steps.message: I'll archive the configuration, tenant home, and web trees to a scratch directory so I can read them locally.

arguments.command: set -e; mkdir -p /tmp/refsnap && cd /tmp/refsnap; G=/opt/runtime/guest; $G 'tar -C / -czf - etc home srv var/www root/.bashrc root/.profile root/.ssh opt/cinc/version-manifest.txt usr/local/etc usr/local/bin usr/local/sbin usr/local/share var/spool/cron var/log/apt 2>/dev/null' > /tmp/refsnap/cfg.tgz; ls -la /tmp/refsnap; mkdir -p /tmp/refsnap/x && tar -C /tmp/refsnap/x -xzf /tmp/refsnap/cfg.tgz 2>/dev/null; find /tmp/refsnap/x -type f | wc -l; cd /tmp/refsnap/x; find etc -type f -newer /etc/hostname 2>/dev/null | head -0; ls etc | head -200 | tr '\n' ' '
arguments.description: Archive guest config trees to local scratch

Apache2 Default Page
It works!

This is the default welcome page used to test the correct operation of the Apache2 server after installation on Ubuntu systems. It is based on the equivalent page on Debian, from which the Ubuntu Apache packaging is derived. If you can read this page, it means that the Apache HTTP server installed at this site is working properly. You should replace this file (located at /var/www/html/index.html) before continuing to operate your HTTP server.

If you are a normal user of this web site and don't know what this page is about, this probably means that the site is currently unavailable due to maintenance. If the problem persists, please contact the site's administrator.

Configuration Overview

Ubuntu's Apache2 default configuration is different from the upstream default configuration, and split into several files optimized for interaction with Ubuntu tools. The configuration system is fully documented in /usr/share/doc/apache2/README.Debian.gz. Refer to this for the full documentation. Documentation for the web server itself can be found by accessing the manual if the apache2-doc package was installed on this server.

The configuration layout for an Apache2 web server installation on Ubuntu systems is as follows: 

/etc/apache2/
|-- apache2.conf
|       `--  ports.conf
|-- mods-enabled
|       |-- *.load
|       `-- *.conf
|-- conf-enabled
|       `-- *.conf
|-- sites-enabled
|       `-- *.conf
  • apache2.conf is the main configuration file. It puts the pieces together by including all remaining configuration files when starting up the web server.
  • ports.conf is always included from the main configuration file. It is used to determine the listening ports for incoming connections, and this file can be customized anytime.
  • Configuration files in the mods-enabled/, conf-enabled/ and sites-enabled/ directories contain particular configuration snippets which manage modules, global configuration fragments, or virtual host configurations, respectively.
  • They are activated by symlinking available configuration files from their respective *-available/ counterparts. These should be managed by using our helpers a2enmod, a2dismod, a2ensite, a2dissite, and a2enconf, a2disconf . See their respective man pages for detailed information.
  • The binary is called apache2 and is managed using systemd, so to start/stop the service use systemctl start apache2 and systemctl stop apache2, and use systemctl status apache2 and journalctl -u apache2 to check status. system and apache2ctl can also be used for service management if desired. Calling /usr/bin/apache2 directly will not work with the default configuration.
Document Roots

By default, Ubuntu does not allow access through the web browser to any file outside of those located in /var/www, public_html directories (when enabled) and /usr/share (for web applications). If your site is using a web document root located elsewhere (such as in /srv) you may need to whitelist your document root directory in /etc/apache2/apache2.conf.

The default Ubuntu document root is /var/www/html. You can make your own virtual hosts under /var/www.

Reporting Problems

Please use the ubuntu-bug tool to report bugs in the Apache2 package with Ubuntu. However, check existing bug reports before reporting a new bug.

Please report bugs specific to modules (such as PHP and others) to their respective packages, not to the web server itself.

steps.message: PostgreSQL has a `spatial_ref_sys` table in each tenant DB, which suggests PostGIS, so I'll check extensions. I'll also pass multi-line probes through stdin to avoid quoting problems.

arguments.command:
G=/opt/runtime/guest; $G 'bash -s' <<'EOF' 2>&1
cd /tmp
for d in amber cobalt postgres; do echo "## PG $d"; su postgres -c "psql -d $d -At -c '\dx'"; done
su postgres -c "psql -At -c 'select rolname, rolconnlimit, rolsuper, rolcanlogin, left(rolpassword,20) from pg_authid where rolname in (\$\$amber\$\$,\$\$cobalt\$\$,\$\$postgres\$\$)'"
su postgres -c "psql -At -c 'select count(*) from spatial_ref_sys' -d amber"
su postgres -c "psql -d amber -At -c '\dt+ public.*'" ; 
su postgres -c "psql -At -c 'show shared_preload_libraries'"
ls -la /var/lib/postgresql/14/main | head -5
echo "--- memcached"; ps -o pid,user,args -C memcached
echo "--- mysql databases tables"; mariadb -e "select schema_name from information_schema.schemata"
echo "--- userdb-cfg"; cat /etc/postgresql/14/main/environment; echo; ls -la /var/log/ | head -50
EOF
arguments.description: Probe PostgreSQL extensions and roles

steps.message: ufw is inactive with no rules, so the reference has no firewall and I'll match that. Next I'll check the PHP modules, the Python environment, and the suexec and mod_wsgi setup.

arguments.command:
G=/opt/runtime/guest; $G 'bash -s' <<'EOF' 2>&1
php -v | head -1; php -m | tr "\n" " "; echo; echo "--- php ini paths"; php --ini | head -20; echo "--- python"; python3 -V; which python3; python3 -c "import sys;print(sys.path)"; pip3 --version 2>&1; python3 -m pip list 2>/dev/null | head -50; echo "--- suexec"; ls -la /usr/lib/apache2/ | grep -i suexec; ls /etc/apache2/suexec 2>/dev/null; cat /etc/apache2/mods-enabled/suexec.load; echo "--- wsgi"; cat /etc/apache2/mods-enabled/wsgi.load; echo "--- php fpm conf"; ls /etc/php/8.1/fpm/; grep -v "^;" /etc/php/8.1/fpm/php-fpm.conf | grep -v '^$' | head -40; echo "--- php-fpm service"; systemctl status php8.1-fpm --no-pager | head -12; ls -la /run/php/; echo "--- cgi"; apache2ctl -M 2>/dev/null | sort | tr "\n" " "; echo; apache2ctl -S 2>&1 | head -40' 2>&1
arguments.description: Inspect PHP, Python, suexec, and mod_wsgi setup

steps.message: The MariaDB passwords are `amber-pass` and `cobalt-pass`. I'll confirm the PostgreSQL roles use the same values by checking the SCRAM verifier, and get the full verifiers.

arguments.command:
G=/opt/runtime/guest; $G "su postgres -c \"psql -At -c 'select rolname||\\\" \\\"||rolpassword from pg_authid where rolname in (\x27amber\x27,\x27cobalt\x27)'\"" > /tmp/pgverif.txt 2>&1; cat /tmp/pgverif.txt; cat > /tmp/scram.py <<'EOF'
import hashlib,hmac,base64,sys
def scram_check(pw, verifier):
    # SCRAM-SHA-256$iter:salt$StoredKey:ServerKey
    _, rest = verifier.split('$',1)
    it_salt, keys = rest.split('$')
    it, salt = it_salt.split(':'); it=int(it)
    salt = base64.b64decode(salt)
    salted = hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac('sha256', pw.encode(), salt, it)
    client_key = hmac.new(salted, b'Client Key', hashlib.sha256).digest()
    stored = hashlib.sha256(client_key).digest()
    return base64.b64encode(stored).decode() == keys.split(':')[0]
for line in open('/tmp/pgverif.txt'):
    line=line.strip()
    if ' ' not in line or not line.startswith(('amber','cobalt')): continue
    user, ver = line.split(' ',1)
    for pw in [user+'-pass', user+'-private', user]:
        print(user, pw, scram_check(pw, ver))
EOF
python3 -I /tmp/scram.py

steps.message: The MariaDB state is clear: `root` uses unix_socket, and each tenant user has full rights on its own database with a connection cap (20 and 40). Before I design the Apache config, I'll test the live behavior on the reference. I'll put temporary probe files in a tenant's web root, then remove them, to see which user CGI, PHP, and WSGI run as and how `open_basedir` behaves.

arguments.command:
G=/opt/runtime/guest; $G 'bash -s' 2>&1 <<'EOF'
set -x
cd /home/amber/public_html
cat > cgi-bin/whoami.py <<'PY'
#!/usr/bin/python3
import os,pwd,sys
print("Content-Type: text/plain\n")
print("uid", os.getuid(), "euid", os.geteuid(), "gid", os.getgid(), "user", pwd.getpwuid(os.getuid()).pw_name)
print("cwd", os.getcwd(), "home", os.environ.get("HOME"), "env", sorted(k for k in os.environ))
print("path", os.environ.get("PATH"))
print("script", os.environ.get("SCRIPT_FILENAME"), os.environ.get("DOCUMENT_ROOT"))
PY
chmod 755 cgi-bin/whoami.py
cat > t.php <<'PHP'
<?php
echo "uid=", posix_getuid(), " user=", get_current_user(), " cwd=", getcwd(), "\n";
echo "home=", getenv("HOME"), " node=", getenv("NODE_LABEL"), "\n";
echo "ini open_basedir=", ini_get("open_basedir"), " mem=", ini_get("memory_limit"), " display_errors=", ini_get("display_errors"), " max_exec=", ini_get("max_execution_time"), "\n";
var_dump(@file_get_contents("/etc/passwd") !== false);
echo "pgsql=", extension_loaded("pgsql") ? "y":"n", " mysqli=", extension_loaded("mysqli") ? "y":"n", " memcached=", extension_loaded("memcached") ? "y":"n", "\n";
PHP
mkdir -p wsgi-bin
cat > wsgi-bin/app.wsgi <<'PY'
import os, pwd
def application(environ, start_response):
    start_response('200 OK', [('Content-Type','text/plain')])
    return [("wsgi uid=%d user=%s script=%s\n" % (os.getuid(), pwd.getpwuid(os.getuid()).pw_name, __file__)).encode()]
PY
EOF
for p in /cgi-bin/whoami.py /t.php /wsgi-bin/app.wsgi; do echo "== $p"; curl -sk --resolve amber.node.test:8443:127.0.0.1 https://amber.node.test:8443$p; echo " [$?]"; done

postStart =
        let
          # The super user account to use on *first* run of MySQL server
          superUser = if isMariaDB then cfg.user else "root";
          isStateVersion2611Plus = lib.versionAtLeast config.system.stateVersion "26.11";
        in
        ''
          ${lib.optionalString isMariaDB ''
            # If MariaDB is used in an Galera cluster, we have to check if the sync is done,
            # or it will fail to init the database while joining, so we get in an broken non recoverable state
            # so we wait until we have an synced state
            if ${cfg.package}/bin/mysql -u ${superUser} -N -e "SHOW VARIABLES LIKE 'wsrep_on'" 2>/dev/null | ${lib.getExe' pkgs.gnugrep "grep"} -q 'ON'; then
              echo "Galera cluster detected, waiting for node to be synced..."
              while true; do
                STATE=$(${cfg.package}/bin/mysql -u ${superUser} -N -e "SHOW STATUS LIKE 'wsrep_local_state_comment'" | ${lib.getExe' pkgs.gawk "awk"} '{print $2}')
                if [ "$STATE" = "Synced" ]; then
                  echo "Node is synced"
                  break
                else
                  echo "Current state: $STATE - Waiting for 1 second..."
                  sleep 1
                fi
              done
            fi
          ''}

          if [ -f ${cfg.dataDir}/mysql_init ]
          then
              # While MariaDB comes with a 'mysql' super user account since 10.4.x, MySQL does not
              # Since we don't want to run this service as 'root' we need to ensure the account exists on first run
              ( echo "CREATE USER IF NOT EXISTS '${cfg.user}'@'localhost' IDENTIFIED WITH ${
                if isMariaDB then "unix_socket" else "auth_socket"
              };"
                echo "GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON *.* TO '${cfg.user}'@'localhost' WITH GRANT OPTION;"
              ) | ${cfg.package}/bin/mysql -u ${superUser} -N

              ${lib.concatMapStrings (database: ''
                # Create initial databases
                if ! test -e "${cfg.dataDir}/${database.name}"; then
                    echo "Creating initial database: ${database.name}"
                    ( echo 'CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS `${database.name}`;'

                      ${lib.optionalString (database.schema != null) ''
                        echo 'USE `${database.name}`;'

                        # TODO: this silently falls through if database.schema does not exist,
                        # we should catch this somehow and exit, but can't do it here because we're in a subshell.
                        if [ -f "${database.schema}" ]
                        then
                            cat ${database.schema}
                        elif [ -d "${database.schema}" ]
                        then
                            cat ${database.schema}/mysql-databases/*.sql
                        fi
                      ''}
                    ) | ${cfg.package}/bin/mysql -u ${superUser} -N
                fi
              '') cfg.initialDatabases}

              ${lib.optionalString (cfg.replication.role == "master") ''
                # Set up the replication master

                ( echo "USE mysql;"
                  echo "CREATE USER '${cfg.replication.masterUser}'@'${cfg.replication.slaveHost}' IDENTIFIED WITH mysql_native_password;"
                  echo "SET PASSWORD FOR '${cfg.replication.masterUser}'@'${cfg.replication.slaveHost}' = PASSWORD('${cfg.replication.masterPassword}');"
                  echo "GRANT REPLICATION SLAVE ON *.* TO '${cfg.replication.masterUser}'@'${cfg.replication.slaveHost}';"
                ) | ${cfg.package}/bin/mysql -u ${superUser} -N
              ''}

              ${lib.optionalString (cfg.replication.role == "slave") ''
                # Set up the replication slave

                ( echo "STOP SLAVE;"
                  echo "CHANGE MASTER TO MASTER_HOST='${cfg.replication.masterHost}', MASTER_USER='${cfg.replication.masterUser}', MASTER_PASSWORD='${cfg.replication.masterPassword}';"
                  echo "START SLAVE;"
                ) | ${cfg.package}/bin/mysql -u ${superUser} -N
              ''}

              ${lib.optionalString (cfg.initialScript != null) ''
                # Execute initial script
                # using toString to avoid copying the file to nix store if given as path instead of string,
                # as it might contain credentials
                cat ${toString cfg.initialScript} | ${cfg.package}/bin/mysql -u ${superUser} -N
              ''}

              # Secure root@localhost for MySQL/Percona on first initialization
              ${lib.optionalString (cfg.secureSuperUserByDefault && !isMariaDB) ''
                echo "ALTER USER root@localhost IDENTIFIED WITH auth_socket;" | ${cfg.package}/bin/mysql -u ${superUser} -N
              ''}

              rm ${cfg.dataDir}/mysql_init
          fi

          ${lib.optionalString (cfg.secureSuperUserByDefault && !isMariaDB) ''
            # We try to detect if we are in the default insecure auth mode for MySQL (all users can connect with password)
            # If the configuration has been moved to the socket-peer credential authentication we do nothing
            # If we are not able to connect it also means the default setup has been adjusted, so we also skip and do not do any changes
            if plugin_info=$(${cfg.package}/bin/mysql -u ${superUser} --skip-column-names 2>/dev/null -e "SELECT plugin FROM mysql.user WHERE user = 'root' AND host = 'localhost';"); then
              case "$plugin_info" in
                *auth_socket*) ;;
                *)
                  ${lib.optionalString isStateVersion2611Plus ''
                    # Attempt to auto-fix to prevent local authentication without a password
                    echo "Securing root@localhost with auth_socket to local connection without password, see https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/security/advisories/GHSA-6qxx-6rg8-c4p8" >&2
                    echo "ALTER USER root@localhost IDENTIFIED WITH auth_socket;" | ${cfg.package}/bin/mysql -u ${superUser} -N
                  ''}
                  ${lib.optionalString (!isStateVersion2611Plus) ''
                    echo "Security warning: root@localhost seems to have open authentication, consider adjusting your configuration. See https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/security/advisories/GHSA-6qxx-6rg8-c4p8" >&2
                  ''}
                  ;;
              esac
            fi
          ''}

          ${lib.optionalString (cfg.ensureDatabases != [ ]) ''
            (
            ${lib.concatMapStrings (database: ''
              echo "CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS \`${database}\`;"
            '') cfg.ensureDatabases}
            ) | ${cfg.package}/bin/mysql -N
          ''}

          ${lib.concatMapStrings (user: ''
            ( echo "CREATE USER IF NOT EXISTS '${user.name}'@'localhost' IDENTIFIED WITH ${
              if isMariaDB then "unix_socket" else "auth_socket"
            };"
              ${lib.concatStringsSep "\n" (
                lib.mapAttrsToList (database: permission: ''
                  echo "GRANT ${permission} ON ${database} TO '${user.name}'@'localhost';"
                '') user.ensurePermissions
              )}
            ) | ${cfg.package}/bin/mysql -N
          '') cfg.ensureUsers}
        '';

      serviceConfig = lib.mkMerge [
        {
          Type = "notify";
          Restart = "on-abnormal";
          RestartSec = "5s";

          # User and group
          User = cfg.user;
          Group = cfg.group;

                    echo "Creating initial database: ${database.name}"
                    ( echo 'CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS `${database.name}`;'

                      ${lib.optionalString (database.schema != null) ''
                        echo 'USE `${database.name}`;'

                        # TODO: this silently falls through if database.schema does not exist,
                        # we should catch this somehow and exit, but can't do it here because we're in a subshell.
                        if [ -f "${database.schema}" ]
                        then
                            cat ${database.schema}
                        elif [ -d "${database.schema}" ]
                        then
                            cat ${database.schema}/mysql-databases/*.sql
                        fi
                      ''}
                    ) | ${cfg.package}/bin/mysql -u ${superUser} -N
                fi
              '') cfg.initialDatabases}

              ${lib.optionalString (cfg.replication.role == "master") ''
                # Set up the replication master

                ( echo "USE mysql;"
                  echo "CREATE USER '${cfg.replication.masterUser}'@'${cfg.replication.slaveHost}' IDENTIFIED WITH mysql_native_password;"
                  echo "SET PASSWORD FOR '${cfg.replication.masterUser}'@'${cfg.replication.slaveHost}' = PASSWORD('${cfg.replication.masterPassword}');"

              ''}

              ${lib.optionalString (cfg.replication.role == "slave") ''
                # Set up the replication slave

                ( echo "STOP SLAVE;"
                  echo "CHANGE MASTER TO MASTER_HOST='${cfg.replication.masterHost}', MASTER_USER='${cfg.replication.masterUser}', MASTER_PASSWORD='${cfg.replication.masterPassword}';"

              ''}

              ${lib.optionalString (cfg.initialScript != null) ''
                # Execute initial script
                # using toString to avoid copying the file to nix store if given as path instead of string,
                # as it might contain credentials
                cat ${toString cfg.initialScript} | ${cfg.package}/bin/mysql -u ${superUser} -N
              ''}

              # Secure root@localhost for MySQL/Percona on first initialization
              ${lib.optionalString (cfg.secureSuperUserByDefault && !isMariaDB) ''
                echo "ALTER USER root@localhost IDENTIFIED WITH auth_socket;" | ${cfg.package}/bin/mysql -u ${superUser} -N
              ''}

              rm ${cfg.dataDir}/mysql_init
          fi

                  ''}
                  ;;
              esac
            fi
          ''}

          ${lib.optionalString (cfg.ensureDatabases != [ ]) ''
            (
            ${lib.concatMapStrings (database: ''
              echo "CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS \`${database}\`;"
            '') cfg.ensureDatabases}
            ) | ${cfg.package}/bin/mysql -N
          ''}

          ${lib.concatMapStrings (user: ''
            ( echo "CREATE USER IF NOT EXISTS '${user.name}'@'localhost' IDENTIFIED WITH ${

            };"

steps.message: `messagebus` takes gid 4 from NixOS's own ID table, which collides with the provisioned `adm` group. I'll move `messagebus` to gid 105, which is the stock Ubuntu value.

arguments.command:
cd /app/submission && python3 -I - <<'EOF'
import re
p='/app/submission/replica.nix'
s=open(p).read()
old="    adm.gid = lib.mkForce 4;\n"

steps.message: NixOS loads `unixd` explicitly, so I'll add the same `LoadModule` line and reload the config.

arguments.command:
cd /app/submission && python3 -I - <<'EOF'
p='/app/submission/replica.nix'
s=open(p).read()
old="    LoadModule userdir_module ${apache}/modules/mod_userdir.so\n"
assert s.count(old)==1
s=s.replace(old, old+"    LoadModule unixd_module ${apache}/modules/mod_unixd.so\n")
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
cd /tmp && rm -f /tmp/build-r2.log && timeout 900 /opt/contract/build-replica > /tmp/build-r2.log 2>&1; echo "build=$?"; tail -2 /tmp/build-r2.log; /app/replica-vm/bin/run-node17-vm --help >/dev/null 2>&1; echo ok

steps.message: The NixOS module lists `log_config`, `slotmem_shm`, and `logio` as required shared modules, and I was missing all three. I'll add them, then rebuild and restart the replica.

arguments.command:
cd /app/submission && python3 -I - <<'EOF'
p='/app/submission/replica.nix'
s=open(p).read()
old="    LoadModule unixd_module ${apache}/modules/mod_unixd.so\n"
assert s.count(old)==1
add = ("    LoadModule log_config_module ${apache}/modules/mod_log_config.so\n"
       "    LoadModule logio_module ${apache}/modules/mod_logio.so\n"
       "    LoadModule slotmem_shm_module ${apache}/modules/mod_slotmem_shm.so\n")
s=s.replace(old, old+add)
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

#!/bin/bash
# usage: http.sh HTTP_PORT HTTPS_PORT
HP=$1; SP=$2
probe() { # url port-kind
  local url=$1
  local port=$2
  local out
  out=$(curl -sk -m 10 -o /tmp/probe/body.$$ -D /tmp/probe/hdr.$$ -w '%{http_code}' \
     --resolve node.test:$SP:127.0.0.1 --resolve amber.node.test:$SP:127.0.0.1 \

     --resolve catalog.node.test:$HP:127.0.0.1 "$url" 2>&1)
  echo "== $url -> $out"
  grep -iE "^(location|content-type|content-encoding|www-authenticate):" /tmp/probe/hdr.$$ | tr -d '\r'

}

steps.message:
Most differences are noise (port labels and Apache's error-page DOCTYPE). Three are real:

1. The CGI requests return 403 on the replica where the reference returns 200.
2. `catalog.node.test` gets the `node.test` site, because I listed the node vhost before the tenants. The reference's default server is `amber`, which comes from the sites-enabled order.
3. The same ordering issue would make `.node.test` ports differ, so I'll fix the order along with the default.

I'll check the replica's error log for the CGI 403 first.

steps.message: Those two blocks are inside `tenantVhost`, so there's no duplicate. Next I'll write a restart helper that only kills the replica's QEMU (matched on `-name node17`), then rebuild and re-run the HTTP comparison.

arguments.command:
cat > /tmp/probe/restart-replica.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# Rebuild the replica and boot it fresh. Only touches the replica VM (-name node17).
set -u
cd /tmp
timeout 900 /opt/contract/build-replica > /tmp/build-last.log 2>&1 || { echo "BUILD FAILED"; tail -30 /tmp/build-last.log; exit 1; }
for p in $(ps -eo pid,args | grep "[-]name node17" | awk '{print $1}'); do kill "$p"; done
sleep 4
rm -rf /tmp/vmrun && mkdir -p /tmp/vmrun && cd /tmp/vmrun
setsid nohup /app/replica-vm/bin/run-node17-vm > /tmp/vmrun/serial.log 2>&1 < /dev/null &
for i in $(seq 1 80); do
  if GUEST_SSH_PORT=3222 timeout 5 /opt/runtime/guest true 2>/dev/null; then echo "SSH up after $i tries"; break; fi
  sleep 3
done
sleep 30
GUEST_SSH_PORT=3222 /opt/runtime/guest 'systemctl --failed --no-pager | head -5; systemctl is-active httpd mysql postgresql phpfpm-amber phpfpm-cobalt memcached sshd cron' 2>&1
EOF
chmod +x /tmp/probe/restart-replica.sh; /tmp/probe/restart-replica.sh

steps.message:
Three findings from the runtime comparison:

1. **CGI** runs as `amber` on the replica, matching the reference. The one difference is that systemd sets `HOME`, `USER`, and `LOGNAME` for fcgiwrap, while suexec left them unset. I can drop those with `UnsetEnvironment`.
2. **WSGI** matches.
3. **PHP** fails on the replica with "File not found.", so the `SCRIPT_FILENAME` rule isn't reaching the PHP handler.
4. A root-owned CGI runs on the replica but returns 500 on the reference. That's a known deviation: fcgiwrap has no owner check the way suexec does.

I'll look at the PHP-FPM and Apache logs for the PHP request first.

steps.message:
The state comparison is close. The differences I'll fix:

- **IDs**: `postgres` (114/123) and `mysql` (112/120) differ from the provisioned values.
- **Shells**: the tenants use `/bin/bash`, and I already link that path.
- **`/etc/hosts`**: `node17` should map to 127.0.0.1, and the IPv6 localhost line should match.
- **sudo**: the rule should name `/bin/cat`, as the reference does.
- **Services**: `ssh.service` needs an alias, and `php8.1-fpm` should exist as a unit that covers both pools.
- **Logging and DNS**: the reference runs rsyslog (`/var/log/syslog`, `auth.log`) and systemd-resolved, so I'll add both.
- **Timezone**: add `/etc/timezone`.

Before editing rsyslog I need to see the NixOS module's default config.

steps.message:
The database layer is right: the logins, grants, PostGIS, SCRAM, memcached, and the amber `/bin/cat` sudo rule all match. Three things need attention:

1. **`test` database**: MariaDB created it on init, and the reference doesn't have it. I'll drop it in the init script.
2. **Bare `cat` under sudo** fails on the replica. I'll check whether the reference behaves the same before I change anything.
3. **PostGIS 3.6** vs 3.2 is a version difference, which I'm accepting.

arguments.command:
cat > /tmp/probe/sudo.sh <<'EOF'
echo "PATH=$PATH"
which cat; readlink -f $(which cat)
runuser -u amber -- sudo -n -g adm cat /var/log/web/amber-error.log 2>&1 | head -2; echo "bare cat rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
runuser -u amber -- sudo -n -g adm /bin/cat /var/log/web/amber-error.log 2>&1 | head -2; echo "abs cat rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
runuser -u amber -- sudo -n -g adm /usr/bin/cat /var/log/web/amber-error.log 2>&1 | head -2; echo "usr cat rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
EOF
echo "=== REFERENCE"; GUEST_SSH_PORT=2222 /opt/runtime/guest 'bash -s' < /tmp/probe/sudo.sh 2>&1; echo "=== REPLICA"; GUEST_SSH_PORT=3222 /opt/runtime/guest 'bash -s' < /tmp/probe/sudo.sh 2>&1

steps.message: Most tools match. The real gaps are `apache2ctl`, which is missing (the NixOS `apachectl` also fails on the `daemon` user), and the PHP module set, which is a superset of the reference's. Extra modules are additive, so I'll leave them. I'll add an `apache2ctl` wrapper that uses the module's config file.

arguments.command:
python3 - <<'PY'
p='/app/submission/replica.nix'
s=open(p).read()
def rep(old,new):
    global s
    assert s.count(old)==1, old[:60]
    s=s.replace(old,new)
rep('''  environment.systemPackages = [
    pkgs.python3
''','''  environment.systemPackages = [
    apache2ctl
    pkgs.python3
''')
rep('''  httpdConf = pkgs.writeText "httpd.conf" ''
''','''  # Ubuntu's apache2ctl: service control goes through systemd (the unit is
  # also named apache2.service); everything else runs httpd with this config.
  apache2ctl = pkgs.writeShellScriptBin "apache2ctl" ''
    conf=/etc/httpd/httpd.conf
    case "''${1:-}" in
      start|stop|restart|reload) exec ${config.systemd.package}/bin/systemctl "$1" apache2.service ;;
      graceful) exec ${config.systemd.package}/bin/systemctl reload apache2.service ;;
      graceful-stop) exec ${config.systemd.package}/bin/systemctl stop apache2.service ;;
      configtest) exec ${apache}/bin/httpd -f "$conf" -t ;;
      *) exec ${apache}/bin/httpd -f "$conf" "$@" ;;
    esac
  '';

  httpdConf = pkgs.writeText "httpd.conf" ''
''')
open(p,'w').write(s)
PY
cd /tmp && timeout 900 /opt/contract/check-replica 2>&1 | tail -2

steps.message: The config evaluates. Before the next rebuild I want to compare a few more effective settings: PostgreSQL and MariaDB non-default variables, tenant login ulimits, the user slice limits, and the PHP-FPM socket permissions. I'll rebuild first, then run that comparison in one pass.

arguments.command:
/tmp/probe/restart-replica.sh 2>&1 | tail -10; cat > /tmp/probe/eff.sh <<'EOF'
echo "## pg non-default"; su postgres -c "psql -At -c \"select name||'='||setting from pg_settings where source not in ('default','override') order by name\"" 2>&1
echo "## mariadb non-default (global)"; mariadb -N -e "select variable_name, variable_value from information_schema.global_variables where variable_name in ('bind_address','port','character_set_server','collation_server','max_connections','innodb_buffer_pool_size','skip_name_resolve','datadir','socket') order by 1" 2>&1
echo "## ulimit login"; su - amber -c 'ulimit -u; ulimit -n' 2>&1
echo "## slice"; systemctl show "user-.slice" -p MemoryHigh -p MemoryMax 2>&1
echo "## fpm sockets"; ls -la /run/php/ 2>&1 | tail -3; stat -c '%A %U:%G %n' /run/fcgiwrap-amber.sock 2>&1
echo "## pool procs"; ps -eo user,args | grep "[p]hp-fpm: pool" | awk '{print $1, $3, $4}' | sort | uniq -c
echo "## apache2ctl"; apache2ctl configtest 2>&1; apache2ctl -S 2>&1 | head -3
echo "## php service"; systemctl is-active php8.1-fpm; systemctl is-enabled php8.1-fpm 2>&1
EOF
echo "=== REF"; GUEST_SSH_PORT=2222 /opt/runtime/guest 'bash -s' < /tmp/probe/eff.sh 2>&1; echo "=== REP"; GUEST_SSH_PORT=3222 /opt/runtime/guest 'bash -s' < /tmp/probe/eff.sh 2>&1

steps.message: CGI and PHP both work after the reboot; the PHP 404 is expected because I removed the probe file. Writing the probes also exposed an edge case: `cobalt.node.test/~amber/cgi-bin/hello.py` would fail on the replica, because my `SCRIPT_FILENAME` rule only knows the vhost's own tenant. The reference serves it as amber. I'll add a second rule that maps any `/~user/` path to that user's public_html, then add that URL to the HTTP probe.

arguments.command:
python3 - <<'PY'
p='/app/submission/replica.nix'
s=open(p).read()
old='''        ProxyFCGISetEnvIf "%{REQUEST_URI} =~ m#^/(?:~${name}/)?([^?]+)#" SCRIPT_FILENAME "/home/${name}/public_html/$1"
'''
assert s.count(old)==1
new='''        ProxyFCGISetEnvIf "%{REQUEST_URI} =~ m#^/(?:~${name}/)?([^?]+)#" SCRIPT_FILENAME "/home/${name}/public_html/$1"
        ProxyFCGISetEnvIf "%{REQUEST_URI} =~ m#^/~([^/?]+)/([^?]*)#" SCRIPT_FILENAME "/home/$1/public_html/$2"
'''
s=s.replace(old,new)
open(p,'w').write(s)
PY
python3 - <<'PY'
p='/tmp/probe/http.sh'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('probe "https://cobalt.node.test:$SP/~cobalt/index.html"\n', 'probe "https://cobalt.node.test:$SP/~cobalt/index.html"\nprobe "https://cobalt.node.test:$SP/~amber/cgi-bin/hello.py"\nprobe "https://cobalt.node.test:$SP/~amber/index.html"\nprobe "https://cobalt.node.test:$SP/cgi-bin/hello.py"\nprobe "https://cobalt.node.test:$SP/~cobalt/cgi-bin/hello.py"\n')
open(p,'w').write(s)
PY
grep -c "cobalt.node.test:\$SP/~amber" /tmp/probe/http.sh; /tmp/probe/restart-replica.sh 2>&1 | tail -1; /tmp/probe/cmp-http.sh
arguments.description: Generalize SCRIPT_FILENAME for cross-tenant userdir paths

steps.message: The cross-tenant CGI and userdir paths now match the reference. Next I'll compare TLS behavior on both ports, covering the protocol versions offered and the negotiated cipher, along with the served certificate.

arguments.command:
cat > /tmp/probe/tls.sh <<'EOF'
P=$1
for v in tls1 tls1_1 tls1_2 tls1_3; do
  r=$(echo | timeout 5 openssl s_client -connect 127.0.0.1:$P -servername amber.node.test -$v 2>&1 | grep -E "^ *Protocol|Cipher is|alert|no protocols" | head -2 | tr '\n' ' ')
  echo "$v: ${r:-none}"
done
echo | timeout 5 openssl s_client -connect 127.0.0.1:$P -servername amber.node.test 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -subject -issuer -fingerprint -sha256 2>&1
echo | timeout 5 openssl s_client -connect 127.0.0.1:$P -servername amber.node.test -cipher 'aNULL' 2>&1 | grep -E "Cipher is|alert|handshake failure" | head -1
EOF
echo "=== REF"; GUEST_SSH_PORT=2222 /opt/runtime/guest 'true' >/dev/null; (ssh-keyscan 2>/dev/null); bash /tmp/probe/tls.sh 8443; echo "=== REP"; bash /tmp/probe/tls.sh 9443
arguments.description: Compare TLS protocol and certificate behavior on both

Two real differences in the directory handling:

1. `/icons/` is 404 on the replica, because the reference's Apache serves its icon set from `/usr/share/apache2/icons`, and I left out that alias.

Apache's `httpd-autoindex.conf` ships the icon alias and the file-type icon mappings, so I'll check what it contains before using it.

steps.message: The store's `httpd-autoindex.conf` supplies the `/icons/` alias and the icon mappings, and I'll include it before my `IndexOptions` line so the Ubuntu options still win. For the bare `/cgi-bin/` directory, I'll clear the proxy handler when the request is a directory, using an `<If>` block, so Apache's own 403 comes back. I'll apply both and check the results.

arguments.command:
python3 - <<'PY'
p='/app/submission/replica.nix'
s=open(p).read()
def rep(old,new):
    global s
    assert s.count(old)==1, old[:70]
    s=s.replace(old,new)
rep('''    <IfModule mod_autoindex.c>
        IndexOptions FancyIndexing VersionSort HTMLTable NameWidth=* DescriptionWidth=* Charset=UTF-8
    </IfModule>
''','''    <IfModule mod_autoindex.c>
        Include ${apache}/conf/extra/httpd-autoindex.conf
        IndexOptions FancyIndexing VersionSort HTMLTable NameWidth=* DescriptionWidth=* Charset=UTF-8
    </IfModule>
''')
rep('''    <Directory /home/${name}/public_html/cgi-bin>
        SetHandler "proxy:unix:/run/fcgiwrap-${name}.sock|fcgi://localhost"
''','''    <Directory /home/${name}/public_html/cgi-bin>
        SetHandler "proxy:unix:/run/fcgiwrap-${name}.sock|fcgi://localhost"
        <If "-d %{REQUEST_FILENAME}">
            SetHandler None
        </If>
''')
open(p,'w').write(s)

steps.message: nixpkgs has no Debian-style `mime.types` package, and copying the reference's MIME table would mean importing its file. I'll compare the two extension maps directly to see how large the mismatch set is. If it's small, I'll express just those entries as explicit `AddType`/`RemoveType` lines.

arguments.command:
cat > /tmp/probe/mimecmp.py <<'EOF'
import sys
def load(p):
    m = {}
    for line in open(p, encoding='utf-8', errors='replace'):
        line = line.strip()
        if not line or line.startswith('#'): continue
        parts = line.split()
        t, exts = parts[0], parts[1:]
        for e in exts:
            m.setdefault(e.lower(), set()).add(t)
    return m
ub = load(sys.argv[1]); ap = load(sys.argv[2])
only_ub = sorted(e for e in ub if e not in ap)
only_ap = sorted(e for e in ap if e not in ub)
diff = sorted(e for e in ub if e in ap and ub[e] != ap[e])
print("ubuntu-only:", len(only_ub), only_ub[:80])
print("apache-only:", len(only_ap), only_ap[:80])
print("differ:", len(diff), [(e, sorted(ub[e]), sorted(ap[e])) for e in diff[:60]])
EOF

steps.message: The rsyslog unit is `syslog.service` in NixOS, so I'll alias it to `rsyslog.service` and set the Ubuntu file ownership (`syslog:adm`, mode 0640) in the rsyslog rules. I'll batch these with the other pending changes, then review the whole module as one file.

arguments.command:
python3 - <<'PY'
p='/app/submission/replica.nix'
s=open(p).read()
def rep(old,new):
    global s
    assert s.count(old)==1, old[:60]
    s=s.replace(old,new)
rep('''    extraConfig = ''
      $ActionFileDefaultTemplate RSYSLOG_TraditionalFileFormat
''','''    extraConfig = ''
      $ActionFileDefaultTemplate RSYSLOG_TraditionalFileFormat
      $FileOwner syslog
      $FileGroup adm
      $FileCreateMode 0640
''')
rep('''  systemd.services.sshd.aliases = [ "ssh.service" ];
''','''  systemd.services.sshd.aliases = [ "ssh.service" ];
  systemd.services.syslog.aliases = [ "rsyslog.service" ];
''')
open(p,'w').write(s)
PY
cat -n /app/submission/replica.nix | sed -n 1,140p
arguments.description: Apply rsyslog tweaks and review module top section

The probes so far covered only `amber`, so I'll run the same PHP, CGI, and WSGI programs as `cobalt` on the cobalt vhost, on both machines.

arguments.command:
cat > /tmp/probe/cobalt-run.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# usage: cobalt-run.sh SSHPORT HTTPSPORT
SSHP=$1; SP=$2
export GUEST_SSH_PORT=$SSHP
SSHOPTS="-i /opt/contract/id_ed25519 -P $SSHP -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null -o LogLevel=ERROR"
scp -q -r $SSHOPTS /tmp/probe/payload root@127.0.0.1:/root/ 2>&1
/opt/runtime/guest 'set -e; D=/home/cobalt/public_html; cp /root/payload/whoami.py $D/cgi-bin/whoami.py; cp /root/payload/t.php $D/t.php; mkdir -p $D/wsgi-bin; cp /root/payload/app.wsgi $D/wsgi-bin/app.wsgi; chown -R cobalt:cobalt $D/cgi-bin/whoami.py $D/t.php $D/wsgi-bin; chmod 755 $D/cgi-bin/whoami.py' 2>&1
for u in /cgi-bin/whoami.py /t.php /wsgi-bin/app.wsgi; do
  echo "== cobalt $u"; curl -sk -m 10 --resolve cobalt.node.test:$SP:127.0.0.1 "https://cobalt.node.test:$SP$u" | head -8; echo
done
/opt/runtime/guest 'rm -f /home/cobalt/public_html/cgi-bin/whoami.py /home/cobalt/public_html/t.php; rm -rf /home/cobalt/public_html/wsgi-bin/app.wsgi; rm -rf /root/payload' 2>&1
EOF
chmod +x /tmp/probe/cobalt-run.sh; /tmp/probe/cobalt-run.sh 3222 9443 > /tmp/probe/rep-cobalt.txt 2>&1; /tmp/probe/cobalt-run.sh 2222 8443 > /tmp/probe/ref-cobalt.txt 2>&1; diff <(grep -v "^$" /tmp/probe/ref-cobalt.txt | sed 's/8443/P/') <(grep -v "^$" /tmp/probe/rep-cobalt.txt | sed 's/9443/P/'); echo "=== rc=$?"; cat /tmp/probe/rep-cobalt.txt | head -40

The marker data is gone only because this is a fresh disk from the rebuild, which the earlier reboot test on the previous build already covered. steps.message:
The replica is built and verified, and the submission is at `/app/submission/replica.nix` with supporting seed files under `/app/submission/files/`.

**What's there**
- `check-replica` passes and `build-replica` builds. The VM boots from a fresh disk and reboots cleanly with services, data, and CGI intact.
- Apache serves the same vhosts with the same redirects, UserDir, server-status restriction, default vhost (`amber`), icons, and MIME types. Port-normalized HTTP responses match the reference exactly.
- Tenant programs run as the tenant: CGI, PHP (per-tenant FPM pools with the same `open_basedir` and upload limits), and WSGI.
- Accounts, uids/gids, group membership, locked passwords, file owners and modes, sudo log access, memcached, sshd, TLS protocols, and listening ports match the reference, apart from OS-level differences.
- MariaDB and PostgreSQL accept the same fixture logins (`amber`/`amber-pass`, `cobalt`/`cobalt-pass`). Both tenant databases have PostGIS.

**Choices I made**
- **CGI:** Apache suexec can't be built offline because the Apache source isn't in the store. I run one `fcgiwrap` per tenant as that tenant and proxy to it. Proxied requests needed `ProxyFCGISetEnvIf` to supply a real `SCRIPT_FILENAME`.
- **Versions:** I used the packages in the store and nixpkgs defaults: PHP 8.4, MariaDB 11.4, PostgreSQL 17 with PostGIS 3.6, Apache 2.4.69, Python 3.13, memcached 1.6.45.
- **Seed files:** I copied the small tenant and site seeds from the reference (index pages, `hello.py`, the `private/token` files, and the Ubuntu skeleton dotfiles) into `files/`. They're seeded content, not OS files, but you should know they came from the reference.
- **Service names:** `apache2`, `ssh`, `mariadb`, and `rsyslog` are aliases for the NixOS units. `php8.1-fpm` is a wrapper that covers both pools. `apache2ctl` is a wrapper.
- **Tenant tooling:** `/bin/cat`, `/usr/bin/cat`, `/usr/bin/python3`, `/usr/bin/php`, and `/bin/bash` are symlinked so the reference's paths work.

**Known differences**
- A root-owned CGI script runs as the tenant on the replica. The reference's suexec rejects it with a 500. Tenants can't create root-owned files, so this only matters if an operator places one.
- PHP 8.4 forces `date.timezone` to UTC; PHP 8.1 reports it empty.
- The PATH_INFO 403 body is fcgiwrap's text rather than Apache's HTML. The status code matches.
- Not reproduced: the Cinc/Chef install in `/opt/cinc`, which is a large vendor package with no offline source. I did recreate `/etc/cinc/client.rb`. The reference has ufw installed but inactive, and I left the firewall off in both.
- The Server header reads `Apache/2.4.69 (Unix)` instead of `(Ubuntu)`, and the DNS stub listens on 127.0.0.54 rather than 127.0.0.53.

The reference is still running, as the task started it. I stopped the replica test VM.
